item.description:
Rubio says no 'breakthrough' in US-Iran talks

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio suggested that there has been no progress regarding truce talks with Iran, accusing the country of making "unacceptable" demands. 

"I don’t have any progress to report to you," Rubio told reporters at the Homestead Air Reserve Base in Florida. "You have a number of countries that continue to engage them with different ideas, but I wouldn’t say we’re on the verge of a breakthrough."

"The president would always prefer to solve this and every problem diplomatically. Sometimes that’s not possible, unfortunately," he added.

Rubio said if there was a chance for a deal, then Washington would "explore it". 

"Right now, it hasn’t been very productive because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable, but in some cases outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic," he said. 

His remarks come ahead of  his flight to Paris, where he is set to attend the G7 Foreign Ministers meeting on Monday and Tuesday.

item.description:
Iran mocks US military initiative to disrupt supply routes

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has dismissed a new US military initiative to restrict the movement of goods through Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea as “merely wordplay”, as tensions over shipping routes and Washington's blockade continue.

“The Iron Gate plan is merely wordplay. The Americans cannot achieve their objectives of imposing severe economic pressure to cause economic collapse in Iran through this approach,” IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi told the semi-official Fars news agency on Sunday, according to Reuters.

Mohebbi said Washington had previously predicted that Iran would suffer economic collapse within two weeks, but that this had not happened.

Tehran had prepared for economic pressure and maintained close relations with neighbouring countries, he said. 

The response came after US Central Command (Centcom) announced the establishment of Task Force Iron Gate on Saturday.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Gaza: Five Palestinians killed as sand embankment collapses on displacement tents
item.description:
Gaza: Five Palestinians killed as sand embankment collapses on displacement tents

Submitted by MEE staff on Mon, 11/09/2026 - 07:57
Three children and two women die in Deir al-Balah as torrential rain and severe weather batter makeshift displacement camps across the Strip
Two women and three children died after a sand embankment collapsed on them in Deir al-Balah, the Gaza Strip, on 8 November 2026 (X)
Off

A sand embankment collapsed on tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in the Gaza Strip late on Sunday, killing three children and two women as severe weather battered the territory.

At least five other people were rescued with injuries by Civil Defence search-and-rescue teams at the makeshift camp in Deir al-Balah, where operations to locate missing people continued.

Mahmoud Basal, spokesperson for the Palestinian Civil Defence in Gaza, said the massive sandy embankment and surrounding mounds of earth collapsed after a low-pressure weather system brought torrential rain and strong winds to the Strip over the weekend.

Two of those killed were identified as Mariam Nabhan and her son, Salah Nabhan. The other three were Reem al-Zain, Habiba al-Zain and Ibrahim al-Zain.

Weekend downpours flooded an estimated 70,000 temporary tents sheltering displaced families across Gaza, leaving thousands of people exposed to the elements.

Palestinians have blamed Israel’s genocide and ongoing siege for the worsening conditions facing displaced people.

‘We do not want to die from the cold’: Gaza families struggle as rain floods shelters
Read More »

“This is not simply the result of severe weather. It is the direct consequence of prolonged Israeli genocide, the widespread destruction of infrastructure, continued displacement, and the denial of essential humanitarian assistance and adequate shelter,” the Palestinian Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Saturday.

The ministry said nearly two million Palestinians were living in approximately 270,000 tents across Gaza in “appalling humanitarian conditions”. 

It added that an estimated 60–85 percent of the tents were worn out and unfit for use, leaving more than 400,000 people exposed to “flooding, rainwater accumulation and coastal hazards”.

Hamas said Israel bore full responsibility for Sunday's “disaster”, citing continued restrictions on the entry of new tents, mobile homes and other shelter supplies.

“The tragedy is a direct result of the criminal policies imposed by the Zionist occupation on the Gaza Strip,” the group said on Sunday.

“The occupation has forced more than two million Palestinians to flee their homes, confining them to less than one-third of the Gaza Strip's territory, in overcrowded areas and shelters that lack even the most basic standards of safety and protection,” it added.

“This makes the recurrence of such incidents foreseeable amid the continued aggression, blockade and severe weather conditions.”

Israeli siege 

Since Israel's genocide began in October 2023, Israeli forces have destroyed or damaged at least 92 percent of homes across Gaza, according to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs.

Israeli forces dropped more than 200,000 tonnes of explosives during almost the first two years of the genocide, equivalent in total energy to approximately 13 Hiroshima-type nuclear bombs.

Almost the entire population of 2.2 million people has been displaced internally, often multiple times. At least 1.7 million people continue to shelter in makeshift camps.

A US-mediated ceasefire agreement in October 2025 was intended to halt Israel's genocide by ending the bombardment and lifting restrictions on humanitarian aid entering Gaza.

However, Israel has continued to carry out near-daily air strikes and demolitions of homes.

Israeli forces have killed nearly 1,600 Palestinians since the ceasefire took effect, according to the Palestinian health ministry.

The overall Palestinian death toll since the genocide began in October 2023 has reached at least 74,600, the ministry said. Thousands more people are missing and most are presumed dead under the rubble.

Israeli authorities have also continued to impose tight restrictions on the entry of aid and goods into Gaza, including essential food, medicines and shelter materials.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Erdogan urges Trump to avoid fresh Iran strikes as Turkey pushes for deal
item.description:
Erdogan urges Trump to avoid fresh Iran strikes as Turkey pushes for deal

Submitted by Ragip Soylu on Mon, 11/09/2026 - 09:58
Turkish intelligence chief says a seven-point deal could avert further US attacks, but warns even a small incident could reignite regional conflict
US President Donald Trump and Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the Nato Summit in Ankara on 8 July 2026 (Ludovic Marin/AFP)
Off

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urged US President Donald Trump over the weekend not to launch another round of strikes on Iran, as regional countries stepped up efforts to de-escalate tensions, Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin said.

Speaking at a conference in Ankara on Monday, Kalin said that Erdogan made the appeal to Trump during a phone call on Saturday. Kalin added that any US attack on Iran would trigger another vicious cycle of regional violence.

Kalin said Turkey and other regional mediators were making progress on a seven-point plan, which he described as a fair agreement.

Under the proposed deal, Iran would receive sanctions relief and gain access to frozen funds. In return, Tehran would commit to not obtaining nuclear weapons and agree to engage with the International Atomic Energy Agency to begin separate nuclear negotiations. Iran would then unblock the Strait of Hormuz, Kalin said.

"It's just a matter of sequencing right now who will take the first step," Kalin said. "That's where we are."

He cautioned that even a small incident could plunge the region into a new wave of conflict.

"If you can get this agreement in the next few days, then there will not be a strike," he said, adding that without a deal, fresh US attacks on Iran could come within days.

Kalin called for greater flexibility from Iran to help move the process forward.

Erdogan is expected to host regional leaders in Antalya on the sidelines of the Cop31 climate summit, providing a potential opportunity to advance the agreement.

He also said Qatar would host US Vice President JD Vance and senior Iranian national security official Mohsen Rezaei next week, describing the meeting as an important opportunity for a breakthrough in negotiations.

Still far apart on deal

An Iranian source familiar with the matter, however, struck a pessimistic tone, saying there was little hope that Washington would move forward with the agreement.

The source told Middle East Eye that Iran expected another wave of escalation soon, which would provoke a forceful response from Tehran against US bases in the region and beyond.

"Trump only understands the cost and we have to make it very costly to him," the source said.

Some Iranian media outlets published footage over the weekend suggesting that Iran could attack US bases in Europe. This prompted debate in Turkey over how Ankara might respond as a Nato ally if such an attack triggered an alliance response.

The Iranian source accused European countries of deepening tensions between Iran and the US rather than helping to ease them.

"We won't target the European bases but the American ones which have been used by the US forces to attack Iran," the source said.

Asked about a potential Nato response, the source said European military capabilities did not exceed those of the US and argued that Europeans should not be concerned because only American bases would be targeted.
